title: The anti-rug dry-run timestamp test runs its own copy of the COALESCE SQL in an in-memory DB instead of the statement in db.ts, so a change to the real statement is invisible (the copy already cites stale line numbers)

evidence.note: "same SQL as src/utils/db.ts:565-572": the statement is re-typed in the test; at the base SHA it lives at db.ts:702-707
src/utils/db is replaced by the in-test copies

sibling_sites_checked: Other mirror-SQL tests: the db/*Migration.test.ts files are checked in Task 2 (RC-28 sibling). preflight/antiRugLiveGate.test.ts reads the value through a mocked getAntirugDryRunStarted (Task 2).
severity_rationale: S3: the mechanism is mocked, but the plausible escaped change (losing COALESCE) makes each restart reset the 7-day dry-run floor, which delays live anti-rug execution (conservative direction); no capital effect.
recommendation: Phase 28: run the test against the real db.ts statement on a temp DB (the rails give each worker a temp DB) instead of a copy.
affected_cases: Test 2: re-calling startChainAntiRugListener for the same chain does NOT overwrite the original ts (COALESCE-idempotent)
Test 4: with fake timers — first call records T0; after advancing 1 day, re-call leaves stored ts at T0
escaped_regression: Drop the COALESCE at src/utils/db.ts:706 (antirug_dry_run_started = excluded.antirug_dry_run_started): every case stays green because the test runs its own statement.
